facts.fact: Lupe 与 Bianca 是「我」母女之外最亲的家人；家族因 Bianca 变性而疏远，Lupe 只要求女儿读完高中、其余随她——两人大致守约。
facts.anchor: Lupe and Bianca were the closest thing to family we had, and though they had a big family of their own, it had thinned out since some of them weren’t cool with Bianca’s becoming Bianca. The first time Lupe ever caught her daughter in one of her slips, she said she could do whatever she wanted as long as she graduated high school, and they both mostly stuck to their word.

facts.fact: 两人合租的 railroad 公寓门在 Mark 卧室：他宁可让室友撞见带人回家也不肯睡进看晾衣绳的小间；这是「我」带女孩回家的测试题——Mark 误引用 Barbra：我们喜欢喜欢人的人。
facts.anchor: Mark would rather have me walk in on him with a lover once in a while than sleep in a closet with a view of the neighbor’s laundry. It worked, somehow. It was a good test for any girl I brought home: If she was fussy about seeing some dick, she was too granola for me. (Mark liked to misquote Barbra: We like people who like people.)

facts.fact: Tanya 送来紫白百合，「我」已预知自己会忘记换水让花枯死；花被摆在 Mark 梳妆台的临时祭坛上，旁边是 Kurt 当年约会时拍的褪色宝丽来。
facts.anchor: Tanya brought an enormous bouquet of purple-and-white lilies and I already felt bad knowing they’d be dead in a few days because I’d forget to give them water.

facts.fact: 众人从 Mark 书架抽他爱的书轮流朗读（Hart Crane、Dickinson、Rimbaud《Illuminations》）；「我」径直翻那本那首「要立恋人为后」的诗——Mark 常念给她听，书脊就在那页裂开。
facts.anchor: I knew that I would find the poem I wanted, the one about the guy who wanted his girl to be queen, because Mark liked to recite it to me, and that’s where the spine was cracked.

facts.fact: Julie 朗读纽约杂志的绅士化报道：赶走租金管制租户、重装、月租七百；人将被推向东河，还要「给他们救生圈」—— she 骂 fucking chilling。
facts.anchor: If you can get rid of rent-controlled tenants, renovate the place, and charge seven hundred a month, it’s worth paying ten thousand or so just to get them out and raise the rents. They’ll all be forced out. They’ll be pushed east to the river and given life preservers.

facts.fact: 守灵夜终于有人挑明：可以谈他死于什么病，不能谈他怎么死的——这种 compartmentalization 让「我」紧张，迟早要漫出来。
facts.anchor: Someone finally brought it up. We were at Mark’s shiva, and we could talk about what had killed him, but not about how he died. Compartmentalization like that makes me nervous—it’s only a matter of time before something spills over.

facts.fact: Star 抛出传闻：有人以「公寓闹鬼」为业上门服务（曼哈顿鬼清除公司）；「我」开始留心听。
facts.anchor: “Whatever they’re called”—Star cleared her throat—“there’re some fucking guys going around convincing people their apartments are haunted.”

facts.fact: Julie 的裁定：她不信鬼，要点是这公司在给人植入「你有鬼」的念头再上门收钱——他们是用 air quotes 说的「替你处理」的骗子。
「我」依稀记起：François 死后门缝下也塞过一张传单；她与 Leon 趁搬运工清走遗物时溜进去拿纪念品——传单上写的像是 rest in peace 之类，当时就让人发毛。
facts.anchor: Then I remembered something, barely: a flyer that had been shoved under François’s door after he died.

facts.fact: 上次见 Claude 的性爱中断回放：第二根手指探入时「我」绷紧——因为一个月前刚死的 François 正站在防火梯上；Claude 看不见鬼，知情者只有 Mark（可能还有 Bianca）。
facts.anchor: The last time I saw Claude, she was easing a second finger into me when I clenched up. François, who had died the month before, was on my fire escape.

facts.fact: 「我」两次试探 Claude 会不会相信自己见过鬼——承认怕、承认认识那个鬼、独自扛。
facts.anchor: “Would you believe me? If I said, Yeah, I saw a ghost on my fire escape and I did freak out, but maybe also I knew the guy, the ghost, and had to deal with it by myself?”

facts.fact: Claude 讲圣文森特医院的病人：痴呆且失明，指着一角空椅说「她是谁——椅子上的女人」，随后描述出他入住前死在那房间的老妇人。
facts.anchor: He says, Who’s she. I ask, Who, he says, The woman in the chair. He was blind to boot, I didn’t mention that. And then, swear to God”—she lowered her voice—“he describes the old woman who’d died in the room before he got there.

facts.fact: 「我」暗自怀疑那个病人就是 François（法国的母亲、明知儿子将死也不来）；她可以告诉 Claude「生病教会眼睛注意缺席」，但证据链不足以说出口。
facts.anchor: I could tell her that maybe the guy was on to something, that maybe getting sick had taught his eyes to notice what was missing. But François couldn’t have been her only patient with dementia, or her only patient with a mother who didn’t love him.
